title: Metric Hypothesis Mapping & Trace Snippet Inventory
content:
Summary:
This is a lightweight planning doc to connect concrete metric hypotheses to the specific trace spans and small trace snippets we'll capture during the metrics sprint. The goal is to produce a prioritized inventory of metrics we can reliably compute from traces and light-weight counters, and produce 6 compact dashboard panels for immediate oncall and rollout needs.

Context & motivation:
- We have many ad-hoc latency and cost panels; investigation often requires stitching traces manually.
- Hypothesis-driven metrics will reduce mean time to resolution by giving operators pre-aggregated signals and trace anchors.
- Focus area for Q1: tokenized inference latency sources (prefetch/kv/cache hits, model-compile stalls, routing fallbacks).

Goals (measurable):
1) Define 12 metric hypotheses with exact computation recipes (query + trace anchor).
2) Instrument two additional span attributes and one lightweight counter for KV warmth.
3) Ship 6 dashboard panels: 3 operator triage views, 2 rollout SLO summaries, 1 cost-per-token heatmap.
4) Create an ownership map and rollout checklist.

Metric hypotheses (compact):
- m1_time_to_first_token_deriv: "TimeToFirstToken" (ms) — p50/p95/p99 from request-start -> first-token-emitted. Aggregation: percentile over 1m windows. Trace anchor: span name "request-processing" with attribute "first_token_delta_ms". Instrumentation: runtime/request_handler: emit attr when streaming emitter flushes. Owner: @Ravi.

- m2_kv_prefetch_hit_rate: "kv_prefetch_hit_pct" (%) — hits/(hits+misses) measured per-tenant per-minute. Aggregation: rate and 1m rolling avg. Trace anchor: spans "kv-lookup" with attribute "prefetch=true" and tag "kv.status": "hit|miss". Implementation: increment counter kv.prefetch.hit/miss in model sidecar on each lookup. Owner: @Ellen.

- m3_dispatch_fanout_latency: "dispatch-fanout-ms" (ms) — time from dispatcher start -> last model-call-start for multi-model fanout. Aggregation: p95 across tenants. Trace anchor: parent span "dispatcher" and child spans "model-infer-call". Note: add ephemeral span attribute "fanout_count". Owner: @Marcus.

- m4_quantization-fallback-rate: "quant-fallback_pct" (%) — fraction of requests routed off optimal quantized path due to compile/compat issues. Data source: routing logs + span attribute 'exec_path'. Alert when >3% sustained 5m. Owner: @Ava.

- m5_kv_eviction_tail_latency: "kv-evict-tail-ms" (ms) — tail latency for requests suffering from cold-kv rehydration. Query: p99 of request latency when span attribute 'kv_warmth'=="cold". Trace anchor: span "kv-prefetch-repopulate". Owner: @Ellen.

- m6_cost_per_token_bucketed: "cost_per_token_usd" (USD/token) — derived by join of billing tokens/time-window with router model-selection. Dashboard bucket by model family and region. Owner: @Finance-observability-collab.

Instrumentation changes (minimal):
- Add span attribute 'kv_warmth' with values {warm, warmish, cold} on kv-lookup spans (serving runtime sidecar). Rationale: allows quick filter for cold-path investigations.
- Emit 'first_token_delta_ms' on response-stream span when first token is sent. Avoid computing in post-processing.
- Counter metrics to expose: kv.prefetch.hit, kv.prefetch.miss, request.streamed_count. Implement as delta counters in the serving runtime telemetry hook.

Trace sampling & cost plan:
- Keep current adaptive sampling but for requests that trigger cold-kv events (kv_warmth==cold) force sample to 100% for 10m windows per-tenant (limited to 50k traces/day).
- Weight traces used in rollout metrics by tenant request volume to avoid noisy low-volume tenants.
- Store synthetic token-level microtraces for 72 hours; full traces 7 days. Long-term retention policy handled by telemetry-archive.

Dashboard composition notes (6 panels):
1) Operator-first triage strip (compact): shows m1 p50/p95/p99, m2 hit rate, m5 p99 cold-latency as single-row microdash with tenant filter. Drill links to top 5 traces (anchored).
2) Fanout heatmap: m3 fanout latency bucketed by fanout_count and model-family (dense heatmap). Use quantile waterfall to surface regressions.
3) Rollout SLO summary: for a given model-version, show m1 and m2 with pass/fail against budgets; show change since rollout baseline.
4) Cost-per-token map: m6 by model family and region; stacked small-multiples for comparison.
5) Cold-kv incident lens: list of recent events where kv_warmth==cold with links to trace snippet and request id.
6) Instrumentation health: shows incoming counts of new attributes (first_token_delta_ms presence rate, kv_warmth adoption %) to validate rollout.

Queries / derivations (high-level examples):
- m1 (first token p95): SELECT PERCENTILE( first_token_delta_ms, 95 ) FROM traces WHERE event = 'request-processing' GROUP BY tenant, 1m
- m2 (kv hit rate): rate(kv.prefetch.hit[1m]) / (rate(kv.prefetch.hit[1m]) + rate(kv.prefetch.miss[1m]))

Alerting proposals:
- Alert A1 (P99 spike): if m1.p99 increases by >30% vs baseline and absolute p99 > 800ms for 5m -> priority P1.
- Alert A2 (kv-prefetch drop): if m2_kv_prefetch_hit_rate < 85% for 10m and trending downward -> P2.
- Alert A3 (quant-fallback surge): if m4 > 3% sustained 5m -> investigate model-compile or kernel mismatch.

Ownership & rollout checklist (minimal):
- Instrumentation tickets assigned to eng-serving-runtime (ensure attr names and small payload).
- Dashboard panels owned by eng-observability with runbook snippets.
- Alerts created in monitoring-alerts repo with pager policy to SRE rotation.
- Staged rollout: dev -> canary tenants (5%) -> cross-region -> global.

Sprint backlog (priority ordered):
- P0: add kv_warmth attribute + counters (1 week).
- P0: add first_token_delta_ms and streaming instrumentation (1 week).
- P1: dashboard panel: operator triage strip (2 days).
- P1: implement m2 kv-prefetch hit rate metric and alert (3 days).
- P2: fanout heatmap (4 days).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How many distinct 'kv_warmth' buckets do we need? warm/warmish/cold seems practical, but might underrepresent medium warms.
- Sampling budget: forced sampling for cold events will increase trace storage — acceptable up to 50k/day; need finance approval.
- Do we compute m6 cost-per-token in telemetry or offline join with billing? Offline gives accuracy; online gives immediacy.

Next steps (this week):
- Finalize attr names in a short RFC (1 page) and link to PR for code changes. (Owner: Ava)
- Create instrumentation tickets and tag them OBS-412. (Owner: Ravi)
- Prototype operator triage panel using synthetic traces and current metrics. (Owner: Marcus)

Notes to reviewers:
- Prefer attribute names that are short and stable (avoid ad-hoc casing).
- Keep per-tenant cardinality low: only attach 'kv_warmth' and 'first_token_delta_ms' — avoid request-level free-form tags.
- If an instrumentation change would add >1KB per span, escalate to architecture review.

References & anchors:
- Linear: OBS-412, OBS-415
- GitHub: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/PR-287 (instrumentation)
- Slack: #obs-instrumentation (thread pinned: "kv-warmth naming")

Appendix: quick-span examples (pseudocode)
- span("kv-lookup", attributes={"prefetch": true, "kv.status": "hit", "kv_warmth": "warm"})
- span("response-stream", attributes={"first_token_delta_ms": 73})

-- end --
